First release. Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners for several repositories of a personal account, all in one container.

## ✨ Added

- One runner per repository in `RUNNER_REPOS`, all in a single container. A personal GitHub account can attach a self-hosted runner to one repository only, and sharing one needs an organization, so the usual images need a container for every repository. Here each repository gets its own copy of the runner, registered under the same name.
- Repositories can be written as `owner/name`, as a full GitHub URL, or as a bare name with `REPO_OWNER` set. Spaces and commas both separate them.
- Stopping the container removes every runner from GitHub again, and the next start registers them anew. The repositories' runner lists never fill up with offline leftovers. `DEREGISTER_ON_STOP=false` keeps them registered.
- A repository the token cannot manage is reported in the log with the reason and tried again after `RETRY_SECONDS`, while the others keep running. A token GitHub rejects keeps the container up, so a corrected token needs no restart.
- A missing token, an empty list or a name without an owner stops the container with one line that says what is wrong.
- A health check that turns red as soon as one of the listed repositories has no runner listening for jobs.
- `RUN_AS_ROOT=false` runs the runners as the unprivileged `runner` user, and with the Docker socket mapped they can still build images and start containers.
- `LABELS` and `NO_DEFAULT_LABELS` decide which jobs may run here. Without the default labels only jobs that ask for your own labels land on these runners.
- The Unraid template gives the container a minute to stop, so removing the runners is not cut short by Docker's default of ten seconds.
- Images for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, built on myoung34/github-runner 2.338.2.
- The build registers a runner in two repositories with a real token, waits until GitHub shows both online, stops the container and fails if either registration is left behind. The test runners carry only the run's own label, so no real job can reach them.
